issues_found.description: Incorrect directory path for Zustand stores - spec referenced 'src/stores/*.ts' (plural) but actual codebase uses 'src/store/*.ts' (singular)
issues_found.location: Lines 67 and 83 in Files to Modify and Files to Reference sections
issues_found.fix_applied: Changed all instances of 'src/stores/' to 'src/store/' to match actual codebase structure. Added specific store names (playerStore, playbookStore, annotationStore, cameraStore) for clarity.

issues_found.description: Research phase was skipped - specification was written without validated research findings, violating the expected workflow where specs should be based on research.json
issues_found.fix_applied: Added transparent note in Overview section explaining research was skipped and technical decisions should be validated during implementation, particularly browser API compatibility.

issues_found.description: Browser API compatibility for requestVideoFrameCallback not addressed - this API has limited support (Chrome 83+, not in Firefox/Safari) without fallback strategy mentioned
issues_found.fix_applied: Added explicit note about fallback to requestAnimationFrame for browsers without support (primarily Firefox and Safari).

issues_found.description: Optional dependencies section unclear about when packages are needed - listed 'may need to install' without specifying conditions
issues_found.fix_applied: Rewrote section to clarify that all required dependencies are already installed. Specified exact conditions when optional packages (video.js, recordrtc) would be needed and emphasized they should only be added if specific browser compatibility issues arise during testing.

issues_found.description: Arbitrary 5-minute export duration limit without justification
issues_found.fix_applied: Added technical justification based on typical browser memory constraints (~2GB for tab processes) and 1080p resolution considerations.

issues_found.description: Inconsistent Three.js namespace usage - code example showed THREE.VideoTexture type but missing import statement
issues_found.fix_applied: Added 'import * as THREE from "three"' to code example to show proper namespace import pattern, ensuring consistency with type annotation.

issues_found.description: Missing Dexie database pattern example - spec mentioned using Dexie multiple times but didn't show the actual implementation pattern
issues_found.fix_applied: Added comprehensive Dexie Database Pattern section with code example showing database class definition, table setup, versioning, and usage within Zustand store. Included key points about extending Dexie class, using TypeScript Table types, and async/await patterns.

issues_found.description: Component directory organization not explained - new VideoImport/ directory introduced without context about existing component structure
issues_found.fix_applied: Added note explaining existing codebase component organization (Scene/, UI/, Layout/) and clarifying that VideoImport/ follows this pattern as a feature-specific namespace.

critique_summary: Spec critique identified 8 issues across accuracy, alignment, completeness, feasibility, and consistency categories. Two HIGH severity issues were found: (1) incorrect store directory path that would cause implementation failure, and (2) missing research validation. Three MEDIUM severity issues involved browser API compatibility, unclear dependencies, and unjustified constraints. Three LOW severity issues related to code consistency and completeness. All issues have been fixed directly in spec.md with appropriate context and justification.
recommendations: During implementation, validate browser API compatibility for requestVideoFrameCallback and MediaRecorder across target browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari)
Test video import and export with various file sizes to determine actual memory limits and refine the 5-minute duration recommendation if needed
Consider adding automated tests for browser API feature detection to ensure graceful fallbacks are working correctly
Monitor performance metrics during development to validate that 3D rendering + video playback maintains target frame rates (30+ fps)
Document any discoveries about video codec support limitations encountered during testing for future reference
